q: The re-order level of a stock item is 950 units. Its average consumption is 70 units per week and the average lead time is 9 weeks. The minimum level (safety stock) of the item is:

options.A: 630 units
options.B: 950 units
options.C: 280 units
options.D: 320 units

q: The annual requirement of a stock item is 7,200 units and orders for it are placed in lots of 900 units each time. The number of orders placed for the item during the year is:

Orders for an item are placed in Economic Order Quantities of 500 units against an annual requirement of 5,000 units, and the cost of placing one order is Rs 120. On the principle on which the Economic Order Quantity is based, the total of the annual ordering cost and the annual inventory carrying cost of the item is:

options.B: Rs 600

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 45 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 280 per unit. The value of the shortage to be brought on record in the stock sheet is:

During stock verification, an excess of 30 units of an item over its book balance is found and is taken on stock after approval. The book rate of the item is Rs 140 per unit. The value at which the excess is taken on stock, through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
A depot holds 750 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 96 to Rs 84 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:

A depot issues 200 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 110 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable, as given, at 12.5 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:

An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 4,50,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 30,000, the insurance premium Rs 7,500 and the customs duty Rs 62,500. The landed cost at which the item is taken into stock is:

A purchase order is placed for 2,000 units of an item at Rs 60 per unit. The Railway later exercises the option clause in the order and calls for an additional quantity of 25 per cent on the same terms and conditions. The value of the additional supply so ordered is:

A stores contract placed at the rate of Rs 500 per unit contains a fall clause. During the currency of the contract, the supplier sells the same item to another buyer at Rs 460 per unit, and 1,000 units still remain to be supplied to the Railway. The reduction in the amount payable by the Railway on the remaining supplies, by operation of the fall clause, is:

A supplier fails to supply 400 units of stores contracted at Rs 180 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made from another source at Rs 225 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:

A railway plans annual procurement of goods and services amounting to Rs 16 crore. Applying the prescribed minimum percentage of procurement to be made from Micro and Small Enterprises, the minimum value of procurement to be made from such enterprises is:

options.A: Rs 3.2 crore
options.B: Rs 4 crore
options.C: Rs 1.6 crore
options.D: Rs 5.28 crore

q: In a stores tender governed by the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, the lowest bid of Rs 10 lakh is from a non-local supplier. A Class-I local supplier has bid Rs 11.5 lakh, which is within the margin of purchase preference. The correct course is that the Class-I local supplier is:

options.A: Given an opportunity to match the L1 price of Rs 10 lakh and, on so matching, considered for award of the order
options.B: Passed over, the order going to the non-local supplier without any opportunity to the local supplier
options.C: Awarded the order straightaway at its own bid of Rs 11.5 lakh
options.D: Debarred from the tender for quoting above the lowest rate

q: A lot of scrap is knocked down in an e-auction on the IREPS portal and the bid is accepted by the competent authority. The purchaser, who has deposited the earnest money, is allowed time to pay the balance of the sale value. That balance is payable by him within:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 21 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 40 days

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The two-packet system of tendering is mandatory for a stores tender valued at Rs 2 crore.
2. The two-packet system of tendering is mandatory for a stores tender valued at Rs 40 lakh.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A firm is the successful tenderer in a stores tender and a purchase order is placed on it. The Security Deposit required to secure due fulfilment of the contract is to be furnished by the firm within:

options.A: 7 days of the placement of the order
options.B: 21 days of the placement of the order
options.C: 45 days of the placement of the order
options.D: 90 days of the placement of the order

q:
Consider the following statements about stock verification:
1. A stock sheet is prepared when an excess of physical stock over the book balance is found, and not only when a shortage is found.
2. Stores found physically in excess are taken on stock, the difference being adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account after approval of the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A depot despatches stores to another depot under a transfer on 28 March. The receiving depot acknowledges receipt of the stores on 4 April. In the closing accounts of the year ending 31 March, the stores in transit stand accounted for in the books of:

options.A: The despatching depot, until their receipt is acknowledged by the receiving depot
options.B: The receiving depot, from the date of despatch itself
options.C: Neither depot, the stores being removed from all accounts while in transit
options.D: The headquarters office, under a separate transit head

q: Material returned to a stores depot by a work is examined and classified as repairable. Such material is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Taking it into stock at once and issuing it without any attention
options.B: Selling it as scrap immediately on its return
options.C: Returning it to the original supplier free of cost
options.D: Getting it repaired, e.g. in a workshop, and taking it back into stock after repair

q: A drill machine and other tools and plant are issued from a depot to a department for use on a work, against acknowledgement, remaining railway property and returnable to stores after use. Such items are borne on the:

options.A: Priced Stores Ledger of the depot
options.B: Dead Stock Register
options.C: Bin Card of the issuing ward
options.D: Stores Monthly Summary

q: A zonal railway is procuring a new item of costly equipment, for which spares will be needed as an insurance against a prolonged breakdown of the equipment. Such insurance (capital) spares for the equipment are ordinarily procured:

options.A: Only after the equipment has been commissioned and put to use
options.B: Only when the equipment first breaks down in service
options.C: Along with the procurement of the main equipment itself
options.D: From the scrap released from similar equipment withdrawn from service

q: Under a stores contract, a supplier's Earnest Money Deposit and Security Deposit remained with the Railways for the full period of the contract. On completion of the supplies, the supplier claims interest for the period for which both amounts remained with the Railways. The correct position is that:

options.A: Interest is payable on both amounts at the bank rate
options.B: Interest is payable only on the Security Deposit
options.C: Interest is payable only on the Earnest Money Deposit
options.D: No interest is payable by the Railways on either amount

q: A supplier offers a depot a lower unit price if an item is ordered in a quantity of 1,000 units instead of its Economic Order Quantity of 600 units. The decision whether to avail of the offer is taken by:

options.A: Always accepting the larger quantity, as the unit price is the lowest
options.B: Comparing the total cost — purchase cost, ordering cost and carrying cost — at the Economic Order Quantity and at the price-break quantity offered
options.C: Comparing only the ordering cost at the two quantities
options.D: Comparing only the purchase cost at the two quantities

q: Stores are issued from a depot to a contractor for use on a railway work being executed by him under a contract. The value of such stores is dealt with by:

options.A: Making no charge for the stores, as they belong to the Railway
options.B: Writing off the value to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Debiting the value, at the rates prescribed in the contract, to the work and recovering it from the amounts payable to the contractor
options.D: Recovering the value in cash from the contractor before any issue is made

q: An engineering (Permanent Way) official requires rails, sleepers and track fittings for the maintenance and renewal of track. Such track materials are ordinarily stocked in:

options.A: P-Way (Permanent Way) stores depots
options.B: Fuel depots
options.C: Imprest stores held by station masters
options.D: General scrap yards

q: A firm pays the prescribed price for the tender documents of a stores tender. It then decides not to submit a tender and claims refund of the price paid for the documents. The correct position is that the price charged for the tender documents is:

options.A: Refunded to the firm, as it submitted no tender
options.B: Refunded to the firm if the tender is discharged without acceptance
options.C: Adjusted against the earnest money deposit of the firm in a future tender
options.D: Not refundable, whether or not the firm submits a tender

q: The Average Annual Consumption of a C-category stores item is put up by a depot for vetting by Headquarters Finance. Under the position after the model SOP of 2018, the correct position is that:

options.A: Vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is required for items of all categories
options.B: Vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is required only for A-category items, and not for a C-category item
options.C: Vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance has been abolished for all items
options.D: Vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is required only for C-category items

q: In the estimates of a work, provision is made for the value of the stores to be drawn from depots for its execution, and the same value is also provided for in the Stores Budget. To prevent the value of such stores being budgeted twice, the Stores Budget provides for:

options.A: A suspense entry
options.B: A transfer entry
options.C: A deduct entry
options.D: A proforma entry in the Works Register

q: A supplier's bill for stores purchased through the Government e-Marketplace is to be processed for payment. The bill is processed through the GeM portal, which is linked with the Railways':

options.A: HRMS
options.B: IPAS
options.C: e-Office
options.D: PRS system of passenger reservations

q: Scrap in a depot is sold by e-auction. The successful purchaser deposits the sale value with the Railways, but delivery of the scrap has not yet been given to him. On the deposit of the sale value by the purchaser, the account credited is:

options.A: Purchase Suspense
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Traffic Suspense
options.D: Sales Suspense

q: A consignment reaches a depot and is physically unloaded, but inspection has not yet been completed. At this stage, the material is treated in the priced stock accounts as:

options.A: Already taken into priced stock from the moment of unloading
options.B: Stock only after it is inspected, accepted and covered by a receipt note
options.C: Stock of the consuming department from the date of arrival
options.D: Scrap awaiting survey by the Survey Committee

q: The Accounts office receives a supplier's bill supported by the purchase order alone; the receipt note for the material has not been linked with it. The correct course is that the bill:

options.A: Is passed in full, the purchase order being sufficient by itself
options.B: Is passed for 98 per cent of its value without any receipt note
options.C: Is not passed until the purchase order, the receipt note and the bill are linked together
options.D: Is paid from the depot imprest pending receipt of the material

q: At the month-end, a depot's position is that several suppliers have been paid for stores which are still in transit and have not been received. This position is reflected in the accounts as a:

options.A: Credit balance under Purchase Suspense
options.B: Credit balance under Sales Suspense
options.C: Debit balance under Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Debit balance under Purchase Suspense

q: A purchaser has deposited the full sale value of a scrap lot, but the lot has not yet been delivered to him. The amount so held under Sales Suspense is finally cleared when:

options.A: The material is delivered to the purchaser and the sale value is adjusted to the appropriate final heads of account
options.B: The next e-auction of scrap is held by the depot
options.C: The purchaser deposits earnest money for another lot
options.D: The financial year in which the auction was held comes to a close

q: A depot finds that it holds serviceable stores well in excess of its own requirements. Before any question of disposal of these stores arises, they are required to be:

options.A: Written off as dead stores by the depot officer
options.B: Sold immediately by e-auction as scrap
options.C: Circulated and offered to other depots and railways which may require them
options.D: Returned to the firms which originally supplied them

q: An item lying in a depot has had no issue for the last 24 months, and the user departments confirm in writing that it will not be required during the next 24 months either. The item is correctly classified as:

options.A: Surplus stores
options.B: Dead surplus stores
options.C: Obsolete stores
options.D: Insurance spares

q: A spare part is in perfectly serviceable condition, but the class of equipment for which it was stocked has been withdrawn and replaced by a new design. The spare part is best described as:

options.A: Dead surplus, because it has not been issued recently
options.B: Scrap, because it can no longer be used in the depot
options.C: Imprest stores of the user department
options.D: Obsolete stores, the design for which it was stocked having been superseded

q: Tools and stores are held in the custody of a user department at an outstation, outside any stores depot. The physical verification of these department-held stores is carried out by:

options.A: Officers of the department which holds the stores
options.B: The depot storekeeper of the nearest stores depot
options.C: The Travelling Inspector of Stores Accounts alone
options.D: The supplier which originally supplied the tools

q: On completion of verification of an item, the stockholder signs the stock sheet recording the difference found. His signature on the stock sheet signifies that he has:

options.A: Admitted personal liability for the difference in every case
options.B: Agreed to pay the value of the shortage in cash at once
options.C: Seen and noted the difference recorded in the stock sheet
options.D: Waived his right to explain the difference subsequently

q: During verification, a shortage of an item is found in one ward of a depot and an excess of the same item is found in another ward of the same depot. In the accounts, these two differences are:

options.A: Set off against each other and only the net difference is recorded
options.B: Both ignored, since they cancel each other within the depot
options.C: Adjusted by altering the bin card of the ward showing the shortage
options.D: Brought on record and adjusted separately, each through its own stock sheet

q: A shortage of stores is established after enquiry, but the enquiry also establishes that the custodian had exercised due care and all prescribed precautions. In such a case, the custodian is:

options.A: Not held personally liable for the loss
options.B: Liable to pay the full value of the shortage in all cases
options.C: Liable to pay half the value of the shortage as a matter of course
options.D: Transferred from the depot as a punishment

q: Coal and oils held in a depot show a shortage which is within the permissible limits prescribed for normal losses in handling and transit of such stores. Such a shortage is dealt with by:

options.A: Recovery in full from the stockholder in every case
options.B: Write-off under the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Debit to the account of the supplier of the coal and oils
options.D: Carrying it forward indefinitely under Purchase Suspense

q: Stores are stolen from a depot during the night. Apart from reporting the matter to the departmental authorities, the custodian is also required to report the theft to:

options.A: The firm which had supplied the stolen stores
options.B: The Stores Tender Committee of the railway
options.C: The purchaser of scrap in the last e-auction
options.D: The RPF/Police, for investigation

q: The custodian of a stores depot is transferred and a new custodian is posted in his place. The incoming custodian takes over the stores:

options.A: Purely on the basis of the book balances, without any check
options.B: After verification of the balances, with discrepancies, if any, brought on record
options.C: Only in respect of the A-category items held in the depot
options.D: Only after the next annual stock verification is completed

q: Material supplied by a firm is rejected at the depot, and the firm does not remove it within the period stipulated in the contract. In that event, the rejected material:

options.A: Is automatically accepted into stock on expiry of the period
options.B: Becomes the personal property of the depot storekeeper
options.C: Is liable to storage/ground charges and may ultimately be disposed of at the supplier's risk, as per the conditions of contract
options.D: Is issued free of cost to the user department which needed it

q: Rejected material is replaced by the supplier with a fresh consignment. Before the replacement consignment is taken into stock, it is:

options.A: Accepted automatically, the original lot having already been inspected once
options.B: Subjected to inspection again and accepted only if found conforming to the specification
options.C: Issued straight to the user department without a receipt note
options.D: Paid for afresh at the full contract rate

q: A supplier delivers a quantity larger than that ordered in the purchase order, beyond any tolerance permitted under the contract, and claims payment for the whole quantity delivered. The excess quantity is:

options.A: Paid for automatically at double the contract rate
options.B: Taken into stock free of cost as a gift from the supplier
options.C: Credited to the personal account of the depot officer
options.D: Liable to be rejected and, in any case, not paid for unless accepted by the competent authority

q: Stores offered against a contract do not fully conform to the specification, but the user department certifies that they are usable for the intended purpose. Such stores may be accepted:

options.A: By the competent authority under a deviation, with a suitable reduction in price
options.B: By the depot storekeeper on his own authority at the full contract price
options.C: Only if the supplier first sells them in an e-auction
options.D: In no circumstances, whatever the user department certifies

q: A tender could not be decided within the validity period of the offers, and a tenderer declines to extend the validity of his offer. In respect of his earnest money, the tenderer is:

options.A: Liable to forfeit it for refusing to extend the validity
options.B: Required to deposit it afresh for the next tender
options.C: Entitled to its refund, his refusal to extend validity carrying no forfeiture
options.D: Entitled to compensation for keeping his offer open so long

q: A tenderer withdraws his offer while the period of validity of his tender is still running. The consequence under the tender conditions is that:

options.A: No action can be taken against the tenderer
options.B: His earnest money deposit is liable to be forfeited
options.C: His offer is kept pending until the validity period expires
options.D: He is paid compensation for the cost of preparing the tender

q: The successful tenderer in a stores tender has furnished earnest money along with his tender. On acceptance of his tender, that earnest money is ordinarily:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railway on placement of the purchase order
options.B: Treated as part payment of his first bill for supplies
options.C: Refunded only after the contract is fully completed
options.D: Adjusted towards the security deposit required to be furnished under the contract

q: A supplier claims interest on his earnest money and security deposit for the long period during which both amounts remained with the Railway. The correct position is that:

options.A: Interest is payable on both amounts at the bank rate
options.B: Interest is payable only on the security deposit
options.C: No interest is payable by the Railway on either amount
options.D: Interest is payable only if supplies were completed before time

q: A successful tenderer proposes to furnish the security deposit required under his stores contract. A form in which it may be furnished, as stipulated in the contract, is:

options.A: A personal surety bond of two railway employees
options.B: A verbal assurance recorded by the depot storekeeper
options.C: A post-dated personal cheque of the firm's proprietor alone
options.D: A bank guarantee, or a fixed deposit receipt, or recovery from his bills, as stipulated

q: The letter of acceptance of a tender is issued to the successful tenderer. The security deposit under the resulting stores contract is required to be furnished by him:

options.A: Within 21 days of the issue of the letter of acceptance
options.B: Along with the tender itself, before its opening
options.C: Only after all supplies under the contract are completed
options.D: Within seven days of the opening of the tenders

q: A contract is expressly placed on firm price terms. During its currency, the supplier claims higher payment because market prices of inputs have risen. Under such a contract:

options.A: The price variation clause applies automatically in his favour
options.B: The contracted rates remain firm throughout and are not subject to price variation
options.C: The rates are revised every quarter by the consignee depot
options.D: The rates follow the market price ruling on each date of supply

q: A supplier realises that he will not be able to complete supplies within the stipulated delivery period. To seek an extension of the delivery period, he should apply:

options.A: Only after liquidated damages have actually been levied on him
options.B: Only at the time of submitting his final bill
options.C: Before the expiry of the stipulated delivery period
options.D: At any time within five years after the period has expired

q: Part of a purchase order has been supplied in time and part remains in arrear and is supplied late. Liquidated damages for the delay are levied on:

options.A: The total value of the purchase order, including the part supplied in time
options.B: The value of the stores remaining in arrear of supply, for the period of delay
options.C: The amount of the security deposit furnished by the supplier
options.D: The value of the stores actually supplied within the delivery period

q: A sum is found due to the Railway from a supplier, but nothing remains payable to him under the contract in which the sum became due. As provided in the conditions of contract, the sum may be recovered from:

options.A: The earnest money of other tenderers in the same tender
options.B: The pay of the stores officer who placed the order
options.C: The sale proceeds of scrap lots held in the depot
options.D: Any sums payable to the supplier under any other contract with the Railway

q: It is established that the tenderers for an item formed a cartel among themselves and quoted collusive rates for it. The tender so received is liable to be:

options.A: Rejected
options.B: Accepted at the lowest of the collusive rates quoted
options.C: Split equally among the members of the cartel
options.D: Finalised after negotiations held with the cartel

q: An offer received against a stores tender contains a material deviation from the conditions of tender stipulated by the Railway. Such an offer is treated as:

options.A: The lowest tender, if its price happens to be the lowest
options.B: Acceptable after imposing a fine on the tenderer
options.C: Non-responsive, and not considered on its merits
options.D: A standing offer to be held over for the next tender

q: After a stores tender notice has been issued, a material change becomes necessary in the conditions of the tender. The change is brought to the notice of all tenderers through:

options.A: A letter sent only to the firm expected to be the lowest tenderer
options.B: An announcement made orally at the time of opening of tenders
options.C: A corrigendum to the tender notice, with suitable extension of the due date where necessary
options.D: A fresh registration of all tenderers for the item

q: A firm has submitted its e-bid on IREPS and now wishes to modify it. Such modification or withdrawal of the bid is possible:

options.A: At any time before the opening of tenders, even after the due date
options.B: At any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders
options.C: Only within one hour of the bid having been submitted
options.D: Not at all, a submitted bid being incapable of any change

q: A firm attempts to submit its stores bid on IREPS after the due date and time fixed for submission have passed. In the e-tendering system:

options.A: The bid is accepted on payment of a late fee by the firm
options.B: The bid is accepted with the approval of the Tender Committee
options.C: The bid is kept pending as an unsolicited offer
options.D: The bid cannot be submitted, the system having automatically closed submission at the stipulated time

q: Samples of oils, paints and chemicals supplied against a purchase order require testing before the material can be accepted. Such samples are tested in:

options.A: The Chemical and Metallurgical laboratory of the railway
options.B: The office of the depot storekeeper
options.C: The office of the Stores Tender Committee
options.D: The laboratory of the supplier alone, whose report is final

q: Equipment ordered by the Railways is still under manufacture at the supplier's works, and inspection is carried out in stages during the process of manufacture itself. This inspection is known as:

options.A: Surprise inspection
options.B: Post-delivery inspection
options.C: Stage inspection
options.D: Stock verification

q: Material offered for pre-despatch inspection is rejected by the inspecting authority as not conforming to the specification. The inspection charges incurred on this rejected material are:

options.A: Borne by the Railway in all cases
options.B: Recoverable from the supplier
options.C: Shared equally between the Railway and the supplier
options.D: Adjusted against the earnest money of the supplier

q: Before a firm is approved by RDSO as a vendor for a safety or critical stores item, it is required to obtain approval of its:

options.A: Annual production programme
options.B: Marketing plan for the item
options.C: Export promotion plan
options.D: Quality Assurance Programme (QAP)

q: A trial order is placed on a firm which has not so far supplied the item to the Railways. The primary object of placing such an order is to:

options.A: Assess the firm's capability and the quality of its product before bulk orders are placed on it
options.B: Enable the firm to avoid payment of earnest money deposit
options.C: Help the firm obtain registration with the Railways
options.D: Meet the annual procurement target from new firms

q: A purchase office places an order on the same supplier, at the same rates and terms as a recent order, for an additional quantity of the same item, without a fresh tender. Such an order is known as a:

options.A: Risk purchase
options.B: Repeat order
options.C: Rate contract
options.D: Spot purchase

q: A stores officer proposes to split a large demand for an item into several small indents so that each part falls within the financial powers of a lower authority. Such splitting of a demand is:

options.A: A recommended measure of economy in purchases
options.B: Permissible with the approval of the depot storekeeper
options.C: Permissible at the level of the depot officer alone
options.D: Not permissible

q: A stores purchase is of small value and falls within the limits laid down in the delegation of powers. Acceptance of the purchase in such a case may be made:

options.A: Directly by the competent stores officer, without reference to a Tender Committee
options.B: Only by a Tender Committee of three members in every case
options.C: Only after obtaining the approval of the Railway Board
options.D: By the depot storekeeper at his own discretion, whatever the value

q: An item is available on the Government e-Marketplace, but a buyer proposes to procure it from outside GeM. Before doing so, the buyer is required to generate on the GeM portal the:

options.A: Tender Committee proceedings for the item
options.B: Proprietary Article Certificate for the item
options.C: GeM Availability Report and Past Transaction Summary (GeMARPTS) ID
options.D: Stock sheet of the depot holding the item

q: Goods supplied through the Government e-Marketplace have been received by the consignee, who has generated the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC). Payment to the GeM seller is released:

options.A: Before the CRAC is generated, on despatch of the goods
options.B: Only after the CRAC has been generated
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year
options.D: Only after the goods are consumed by the user department

q: Stores are imported on F.O.B. terms, under which the price does not cover insurance beyond the port of shipment. The marine insurance of the consignment for the sea transit is therefore arranged by:

options.A: The Railway, as buyer, which also prefers any claim for transit loss or damage on the insurer
options.B: The foreign supplier, the price covering insurance to destination
options.C: The depot storekeeper out of the depot imprest
options.D: The inspecting authority which inspected the stores abroad

q: A foreign supplier quotes a price for imported stores on C.I.F. terms. The price so quoted is distinguished from an F.O.B. price in that it includes:

options.A: Only the ex-factory cost of the material
options.B: The customs duty payable in India on import
options.C: The cost of the material plus the inland freight in India
options.D: Cost, insurance and freight up to the port of destination

q: A depot holds serviceable stores surplus to its own requirements, while another depot has a pending demand for the same item. Before any disposal of the surplus stores is considered, the correct course is that the stores should be:

options.A: Sold at once by e-auction as scrap
options.B: Circulated and offered to other depots and railways which may require them
options.C: Written off from the books as dead stores
options.D: Returned to the firm which originally supplied them

q: During stock verification of an item, the physical balance is found to be in excess of the book balance and there is no shortage of any kind. In such a case:

options.A: A stock sheet is prepared for the excess, as it is for a shortage
options.B: No stock sheet is prepared, a stock sheet being confined to shortages only
options.C: The excess is removed from the depot without any record
options.D: The bin card is altered silently to match the physical balance

q: A stock verifier notices, during verification, that the prescribed procedure for receipt and issue of stores has not been followed in a depot, although no difference in quantities is found. Such procedural irregularities are brought out by the Inspector of Stores Accounts or Assistant Stock Verifier through:

options.A: An error sheet
options.B: A stock sheet
options.C: The Stores Monthly Summary
options.D: A narrative report

q: An item in a depot was last issued thirty months ago. There is no indication that it will be required during the next twenty-four months. The item is correctly classified as:

options.A: Surplus stores
options.B: Imprest stores
options.C: Dead surplus stores
options.D: Insurance spares

q: A depot holds stores in serviceable condition, but a change in the design of the equipment on which they were used has made it impossible to put them to any use. Such stores are correctly described as:

options.A: Repairable stores
options.B: Obsolete stores
options.C: Returnable stores
options.D: Non-stock stores

q: A purchaser has deposited the full sale value of a scrap lot and the amount is held under Sales Suspense. This amount is finally cleared from Sales Suspense when:

options.A: The next e-auction is held by the depot
options.B: The purchaser deposits earnest money for another lot
options.C: The financial year in which the auction was held comes to a close
options.D: The material is delivered to the purchaser and the sale value is adjusted to the appropriate final heads of account

q: At the year-end review of stores accounts, a net balance is found standing in the Stock Adjustment Account after all price and quantity differences of the year have been passed through it. The balance so standing is finally cleared:

options.A: At the close of the year, under the sanction of the competent authority
options.B: By transfer to the Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: By carrying it forward indefinitely from year to year
options.D: By adjustment against the coaching earnings of the railway

q: On periodical agreement, a difference is noticed between the balance of an item in the custody accounts of a depot and its balance in the priced accounts. The correct treatment of the difference is that it should be:

options.A: Adjusted at once by altering the priced ledger to match the bin card
options.B: Ignored, since the two sets of accounts are never compared
options.C: Investigated and reconciled before any adjustment is made
options.D: Written off by the storekeeper without any enquiry

q: A field official holding imprest stores seeks replenishment, but has not rendered any account of the consumption of the stores last supplied to him. Replenishment of his imprest is properly made:

options.A: On the basis of the annual budget allotment alone
options.B: Only after the account of consumption rendered by him is taken into account
options.C: Against a fresh tender invited for the replenishment
options.D: On the basis of a narrative report of the stock verifier

q: The equipment for which costly insurance spares are held in a depot is itself condemned and scrapped, and the spares are not required for any other equipment. The insurance spares should be:

options.A: Retained in stock indefinitely
options.B: Issued free of cost to the depot staff
options.C: Destroyed immediately without any survey
options.D: Reviewed and, being no longer required, declared surplus and disposed of

q: Stores returned to a depot are examined and classified as repairable. Such stores are taken back into stock:

options.A: After they have been made serviceable again by repair, for example in a workshop
options.B: At once, without any repair or examination
options.C: Only after they have been sold and repurchased
options.D: Never, repairable stores being invariably sold as scrap

q: A work returns serviceable material to a depot and claims credit at the full price at which the material was originally issued, ignoring its present condition. The credit to be given to the returning work is:

options.A: At the original issue price in all cases
options.B: At the current market price of new material
options.C: At the value assessed for the returned material in its present condition
options.D: Nil, no credit being admissible for returned stores

q: Stores are transferred from one depot of a railway to another depot which requires them. The transferred stores are priced at:

options.A: The current market rate on the date of transfer
options.B: The book value of the material
options.C: A rate fixed by the receiving depot
options.D: The rate of the last purchase made by the receiving depot

q: A depot despatches stores to another depot under a transfer. In the books of the despatching depot, the stores remain accounted for:

options.A: Only until the wagon leaves the depot siding
options.B: Until the end of the month of despatch in all cases
options.C: Not at all, being removed from all accounts on despatch
options.D: Until their receipt is acknowledged by the receiving depot

q: In an emergency, a depot urgently requiring stores obtains them from another depot on a loan basis. Such a loan transaction means that:

options.A: The material is issued against an obligation to return it in kind or to have its value adjusted, the loan remaining outstanding until liquidated
options.B: The borrowing depot need never return or account for the material
options.C: The lending depot writes off the material from its books at once
options.D: The material is treated as a free gift between the two depots

q: Material received at a depot is found, at the time of receipt, to be short in quantity and damaged. The correct course for the depot is to:

options.A: Accept the consignment silently and ignore the loss
options.B: Deduct an arbitrary amount from the next bill of the firm without any record
options.C: Record the shortage and damage on the receipt documents and prefer a claim on the supplier or the carrier, as the case may be
options.D: Hold the depot storekeeper personally liable without any record of the shortage

q: A consignment has physically arrived at a depot, but inspection of the material is still awaited. The material is taken into the priced stock accounts of the depot:

options.A: Immediately on its arrival at the depot gate
options.B: Only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note has been issued
options.C: As soon as it is issued to a consuming department
options.D: At the end of the financial year in which it arrives

q: A supplier delivers material at a stores depot and is given a receipt at the gate. The nature of that receipt is that it is:

options.A: Final, the material being treated as accepted at the gate itself
options.B: Followed by payment of the full bill amount at the gate
options.C: Not recorded anywhere in the records of the depot
options.D: Only provisional, final acceptance following inspection and issue of the receipt note

q: Stores are purchased on the basis of an approved sample. After the purchase order is placed, the approved sample is:

options.A: Sealed and retained, so that the bulk supplies can be compared with it at inspection
options.B: Returned to the supplier immediately
options.C: Destroyed at once
options.D: Sold along with the scrap lots of the depot

q: Material rejected at destination is replaced by the supplier and the replacement consignment reaches the depot. The replacement material is:

options.A: Accepted into stock automatically without any check
options.B: Paid for afresh at the full contract rate in addition to the original supply
options.C: Subjected to inspection again and accepted into stock only if found conforming to the specification
options.D: Issued directly to the user department without a receipt note

q: A supplier delivers a quantity of stores in excess of the quantity ordered, beyond any tolerance permitted under the contract. The excess quantity is:

options.A: Automatically paid for at double the contract rate
options.B: Not paid for, and is liable to be rejected, unless the excess is accepted by the competent authority
options.C: Taken into stock free of cost as a gift from the supplier
options.D: Credited to the personal account of the depot officer

q: A tender submitted for stores contains a material deviation from the conditions of tender stipulated by the Railway. Such a tender is liable to be:

options.A: Accepted as the lowest tender in all cases
options.B: Accepted after imposing a fine on the tenderer
options.C: Held over for the next tender as a standing offer
options.D: Treated as non-responsive and not considered on merits

q: Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender may be furnished by a tenderer in an approved form, such as:

options.A: Cash, demand draft or pay order, bank guarantee or fixed deposit receipt, as stipulated in the tender conditions
options.B: A personal cheque of the proprietor of the firm only
options.C: A verbal assurance given by the tenderer
options.D: Post-dated cheques only

q: A firm's period of registration for supply of stores to the Railways has run out and its case comes up for renewal. The position regarding the tenure of such registration is that it is:

options.A: Granted once for the entire life of the firm and never reviewed
options.B: Granted only to firms which have never supplied stores before
options.C: Granted for a limited period and renewed thereafter after a review of the performance of the firm
options.D: Not required to be recorded in any register

q: The performance of a registered firm as a vendor is found to be persistently poor. The consequence the firm may face is:

options.A: Automatic allotment of larger orders as compensation
options.B: Down-gradation, suspension or cancellation of its registration
options.C: A fine imposed personally by the depot storekeeper
options.D: No consequence of any kind
